news.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Head of Nvidia
news.description: Jensen Huang reportedly resigned as CEO of Nvidia after reports emerged of two alleged affairs with Chinese spies. Nvidia’s valuation fell by 800 billion dollars following the controversy.

news.title: A Global Microsoft 365 Outage Affects Outlook and Teams
news.description: A global Microsoft 365 outage crippled Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services. Microsoft attributed it to an overloaded secure-connection process and said it was not a cyberattack.

news.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Coding Assistants
news.description: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model designed for coding assistants and software that uses tools. It accepts text, images, audio and video, with adjustable reasoning levels and usage-based pricing.

news.title: Tesla and SpaceX Merger Talks Reach a New Stage
news.description: Talks aimed at a merger between Tesla and SpaceX have reached a new stage, but one obstacle remains.

news.title: Google Unveils Intelligent Eyewear, the Successor to Google Glass
news.description: These new smart glasses let users use Gemini in everyday life to ask questions, take photos and translate conversations. Preorders are open, and deliveries will begin on December 10.

news.title: United Airlines Blocks Unauthorized Personal AI Agents
news.description: United is restricting unauthorized personal AI agents, citing unintended purchases, exposure of account information and regulatory obligations. Analysts note that the lack of consistent standards and the difficulty of distinguishing bots from customers complicate transaction automation.

news.title: Chinese Supplier Confirms Its Involvement in Unreleased Apple Products
news.description: An Apple supplier in China appears to have confirmed its involvement in Apple’s AI glasses, camera-equipped AirPods and other unannounced projects in a financial report.

news.title: OLED iPad Air Expected in Early 2027
news.description: A new report claims that the iPad Air with an OLED display will arrive in early 2027. It is not expected to support ProMotion.

news.title: Government-Grade Spyware Is Now Targeting iPhones
news.description: Researchers say sophisticated spyware previously reserved for government surveillance is being used against private individuals. Two iOS exploit kits, Coruna and DarkSword, are involved.

news.title: OLED iPad mini Review: An Excellent Reader, but Not a Miniature iPad Pro
news.description: The eighth-generation iPad mini benefits greatly from its OLED display, but its price makes it less appealing compared with the iPad Pro. AppleInsider gives it a score of 4 out of 5.

news.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for Its AI Agents
news.description: ChatGPT Wallet lets “dots” AI agents purchase products for users after approval and security verification. Developed with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, the system uses a payment token for each transaction without sharing the actual card details.

news.title: OpenAI Enters the Cybersecurity Market with Two Daybreak Products
news.description: OpenAI is launching two Daybreak products and entering the cybersecurity market.

news.title: Meta’s Muse Can Now Make Calls, but the Feature Costs Extra
news.description: Muse, Meta’s AI, can now make phone calls, but the feature is not free.

news.title: Lawsuit Calls for an End to Frontier AI Development
news.description: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are facing a lawsuit seeking to halt the development of frontier AI systems.

news.title: SpaceX Lays Off 60 Grok Imagine Employees to Focus on AI
news.description: SpaceX laid off 60 Grok Imagine employees as Elon Musk redirects his efforts toward coding and AI agents.

news.title: Silicon Valley Prepares for a Future Without Jensen Huang
news.description: At a major artificial intelligence conference in Silicon Valley, investors and executives are considering a future without Jensen Huang.

news.title: Companies Must Decide Which AI Agents to Allow as Customers or Intermediaries
news.description: AI agents are already buying on behalf of customers, and companies must decide which ones to let access their information, offers and services. OpenAI is opening an official path for businesses in ChatGPT, while United Airlines is restricting unauthorized third-party agents; agentic commerce is thus becoming a distribution strategy.

news.title: Anthropic Introduces Fable 5.2, Faster and Less Expensive to Run
news.description: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 is up to 30% faster than version 5.1. Its standard price is 8 dollars per million input tokens and 40 dollars per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode.

news.title: Google’s 10-Minute AI Training Plan for Marketers
news.description: Google is offering a 10-minute artificial intelligence training plan for marketing teams.

news.title: How Many Physical Keys Should You Get for a Tesla?
news.description: An owner asks how many physical keys it is recommended to get for their Tesla. One response also mentions using an Apple Watch as a backup key.

news.title: Anthropic Turns Claude Into an Active Participant in Video Meetings
news.description: Claude Meetings lets users add the assistant to video calls to follow discussions, take notes and start certain tasks before the meeting ends. The service is rolling out on Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plans, with other platforms expected to follow.

news.title: Wispr Flow Turns Voice Dictation Into Polished Text Across All Apps
news.description: Wispr Flow lets users dictate text in WhatsApp, Slack, Gmail, ChatGPT or a browser, then removes hesitations, corrects grammar and formats the result. The tool is available on Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, with free unlimited access on Android at launch.

news.title: OpenAI’s Personal Assistant Gets Faster Responses and Advanced Settings
news.description: OpenAI’s personal assistant was improved this week with faster responses and more customizable instructions.

news.title: Chatbots Sometimes Recommend Fake Online Stores
news.description: A Podqi test examining where to buy products from 151 brands found that ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity sometimes direct users to impersonator or risky websites. Users are advised to verify a brand’s official address before making any purchase.

news.title: OpenAI Explains Why Its Models Are Hiding More of Their Reasoning
news.description: OpenAI’s safety team attributes the growing opacity of its models’ chain of thought to four stages of training, including architecture and reinforcement learning. This opacity results from trade-offs intended to improve performance and reduce computation.

news.title: Generative AI Use Is Growing Among Video Game Developers
news.description: According to the GDC Festival of Gaming’s annual survey, 40% of developers use generative AI at work, up from 36% in 2025. The proportion reaches 70% at mobile studios, while part of the industry is publicly opposing it.

news.title: Cerebras Stock Jumps After Deal With Microsoft
news.description: The AI chipmaker exceeded quarterly expectations and signed a deal with Microsoft, which joins Amazon and Oracle among its cloud customers. The announcement supports alternatives to Nvidia, despite the stock still being down nearly half since its IPO.

news.title: OpenAI Creates an Official Business Space in ChatGPT
news.description: Businesses can now claim their presence in ChatGPT, update their information and publish Business Agents that customers can interact with. ChatGPT is thus evolving from a descriptive tool into a distribution channel for businesses.

news.title: AI Assistants Become the Upstream Interface for Banking Services
news.description: According to McKinsey, 74% of consumers who use AI for banking tasks rely on general-purpose assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Customers can therefore make a decision before even entering a bank’s environment.

news.title: ChatGPT Becomes a New Gateway to Businesses
news.description: OpenAI has launched Businesses in ChatGPT, allowing companies to manage their presence, product information and customer interactions in ChatGPT. Customer acquisition is therefore beginning to move outside channels controlled by businesses.

news.title: Huang’s Departure Alarms Investors Across the AI Sector
news.description: The Nvidia leader’s resignation is weakening the company’s stock and raising fears of repercussions for companies across the artificial intelligence industry.

news.title: Huang’s Departure Could Change the Outlook for Anthropic’s IPO
news.description: Nvidia’s planned $10 billion investment could be reassessed, while future chip deals could slow. The departure could also strengthen Anthropic’s position in Washington and its chip-diversification strategy.

news.title: OpenAI Security Officials Tricked by Fake Russian Agents
news.description: Three senior OpenAI national security officials spent 17 minutes on a video call with Russian scammers posing as Ukraine’s intelligence chief. OpenAI has opened an investigation and taken steps to prevent a recurrence.

news.title: Groups Call for a Freeze on New AI Models
news.description: Four nonprofit organizations asked a San Francisco judge to halt new frontier models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI.

news.title: OpenAI Reportedly Supports Bills Restricting China’s Access to AI Chips
news.description: OpenAI reportedly told lawmakers it would support bipartisan bills restricting China’s access to artificial intelligence chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO Reportedly Six Times Oversubscribed
news.description: Anthropic’s IPO reportedly attracted about six times more demand than the number of shares offered. During its roadshow, the company also said Claude had been ported to AMD GPUs in three days, compared with several months previously.

news.title: SpaceX Announces $74 Billion in AI Computing Sites
news.description: SpaceX announced $74 billion in investments in AI-dedicated computing sites, including a $50 billion site in Arizona and a $24 billion gas-powered complex near Starbase.

news.title: ChatGPT’s Personal Agents Now Support Custom Instructions
news.description: ChatGPT’s personal agents can now follow custom instructions, such as writing only in lowercase or displaying a draft before sending an email.

news.title: Could the Touchscreen MacBook Pro Replace the M5 iPad Pro?
news.description: The touchscreen MacBook Pro supports macOS apps and offers substantial memory and storage, but it does not work with the Apple Pencil. It starts at $2,899, compared with $999 for the M5 iPad Pro.

news.title: FAA Lifts National Ground Stop After Nearly 5,000 Flights Are Canceled
news.description: The Federal Aviation Administration ground stop, which paralyzed flights nationwide for several hours, was lifted Friday evening. Travelers were stranded at airports, and nearly 5,000 flights were canceled.

news.title: What to Do If Your Flight Is Canceled or Delayed Because of the FAA Ground Stop
news.description: This article explains what to do if the FAA ground stop caused a flight cancellation or delay.

news.title: Passengers Describe the Chaos at JFK During the Nationwide Ground Stop
news.description: Passengers describe the chaos they experienced at JFK airport during the FAA’s nationwide ground stop.

news.title: Photos Show Disruptions at U.S. Airports
news.description: Photos show the difficulties encountered at airports across the country while the FAA grounded all flights.

news.title: FAA Ground Stop Could Disrupt College Football Games
news.description: The FAA ground stop could jeopardize the staging of college football games.

news.title: Toronto and Montreal Declare Ground Stops at Their Airports
news.description: The airports in Toronto and Montreal declared ground stops.

news.title: SMART AI Maker and Microsoft Deny Responsibility for the Ground Stop
news.description: The company behind the SMART AI system and Microsoft both say they were not responsible for the FAA ground stop.

news.title: Apple Tests Harbor to Connect Multiple Macs to Local AI
news.description: The Harbor app, formerly called Fabric, can turn multiple Macs into a private AI inference server. It is currently available as a private preview under the Claris brand.

news.title: Donald Trump Wants Tim Cook to Become Nvidia’s Next CEO
news.description: Donald Trump said Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as head of Nvidia, stating that “a legend replaces a legend.”

news.title: Johny Srouji Could Take Over as Nvidia CEO
news.description: Another report says that Johny Srouji, Apple’s head of hardware, could become Nvidia’s next CEO.

news.title: Unpatched iOS Flaw Could Let Apps Steal Data
news.description: An iOS vulnerability could allow malicious apps to read other apps’ local files by bypassing their sandbox.

news.title: Thai Officials Question Apple About Spyware Alerts
news.description: Thai politicians questioned Apple about its alerts sent to users targeted by spyware.

news.title: iOS 27.2.1 Fixes Bluetooth and iMessage-Related Vulnerabilities
news.description: The iOS 27.2.1 update fixes vulnerabilities that enabled unauthorized Bluetooth pairings and eavesdropping on iMessage messages.

news.title: Apple HomeView Review: A Limited Launch, but Strong Potential
news.description: HomeView is Apple’s first attempt in the smart-home display category. The product shows significant potential but still needs improvements, earning a score of 2.5 out of 5.

news.title: Nvidia Employees Call for Jensen Huang’s Return
news.description: Nvidia employees asked the board to reinstate Jensen Huang after his resignation. An internal post received more than 1,600 comments, while the crisis cost the company 1 trillion dollars in market value.

news.title: China Rents Nvidia Chips Ahead of a Possible U.S. Embargo
news.description: Chinese AI companies are accessing Nvidia’s best chips by renting computing power in data centers in Malaysia and Thailand. U.S. restrictions control where the chips are shipped, but not the identities of the users connecting to them.

news.title: Chinese AI Models Appear to Be Using Banned Nvidia Chips
news.description: A forensic analysis claims to provide the first technical evidence that several Chinese laboratories are using Nvidia Blackwell GPUs subject to export controls. The method relies on a statistical signature left by the number of computing cores, but it cannot determine where the chips are located or prove that they were smuggled.

news.title: HubSpot Brings Back Cofounder Brian Halligan as CEO
news.description: HubSpot is bringing back cofounder Brian Halligan as CEO to “refound” the company.

news.title: Binance Hack Prompts U.S. to Target 1.2 Billion Dollars
news.description: The United States is targeting 1.2 billion dollars in stolen cryptocurrency following the Binance hack.

news.title: Whoop Launches Its Own Social Network
news.description: Whoop launched a social network.

news.title: FAA Expands AI Advice Across U.S. Airspace
news.description: The FAA is expanding the use of AI-generated advice to manage air-traffic congestion across all U.S. airspace.

news.title: The “Slop” Phenomenon Is Moving Up the Value Chain
news.description: The article examines the spread of “slop” up the value chain.

news.title: Nvidia Scandal Involves U.S. Commerce Secretary
news.description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly agreed to testify about Nvidia chip sales to China.

news.title: Automate Your Inbox and Calendar While Staying in Control
news.description: Chapter 30 explains how to automate inbox sorting, draft replies and manage the steps before and after a meeting without allowing AI to send messages or accept appointments without approval. It notably proposes a morning summary that does not modify the inbox and the automatic capture of commitments.

news.title: Jensen Huang Reveals the Risk of Building a Company Around a Single Leader
news.description: The sudden departure of Nvidia’s former CEO highlights the risks of relying on a single leader. Nvidia’s horizontal structure helped it move quickly, but also exposed the company.

news.title: Jensen Huang Is Targeted by the Technology He Helped Create
news.description: The article examines criticism directed at Jensen Huang and the technology he helped bring into existence.

news.title: AI Upends the Economics of Customer Loyalty
news.description: AI enables agents to compare prices, terms and products daily, revealing that some loyalty was based largely on customer inertia. Companies must determine whether customers stay for trust, experience and genuine differentiation, or simply because switching providers is difficult.

news.title: Instagram Launches a Web Tool for Creating Story Effects With Prompts
news.description: Effect Builder lets U.S. creators aged 18 and over generate AI effects for Stories without design or programming skills. Published effects are reviewed and display their creator’s Instagram account.

news.title: Adobe and Disney Partner to Create Custom AI Models
news.description: Disney will use Adobe Firefly Foundry to create models trained on its own characters, environments and visual styles. Walt Disney Imagineering is already using them for theme park development, including turning sketches into rendered 2D concepts.

news.title: Meta Launches Muse Ember, Its Smallest AI Model
news.description: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest model, priced at 0.10 dollars per million input tokens. It is designed for high-volume agent tasks such as tool calls and long-document analysis.

news.title: Google Publishes a Guide to Get More From Gemini 4 Carbon
news.description: Google has published a guide for developers with five practical tips for getting better results from Gemini 4 Carbon on difficult problems.

news.title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok Bot 1.0 for Teams on Slack and Microsoft Teams
news.description: SpaceXAI has launched Grok Bot 1.0, a teammate that works in Slack or Microsoft Teams. It can take on tasks without prompting and share memory across an organization.

news.title: Lessons From Major Companies on Moving Beyond the AI Pilot Era
news.description: The AI pilot era is over. Executives from JPMorgan Chase, Gap, Estée Lauder and other companies share practical lessons for evolving workflows and demonstrating marketing ROI.

news.title: Why 82% of Executives Fail to See Marketing’s Value
news.description: A study examines why 82% of executives miss the value of marketing.

news.title: AI Reduces Friction While Human Expertise Dispels Doubts
news.description: Andy Kurtzig, founder and CEO of Pearl, explains how AI reduces friction and how human expertise helps resolve uncertainty.

news.title: Which Mobile Charger Should You Use at 110 V and 240 V for a Tesla?
news.description: A new Tesla owner is looking for the best portable charger that works at 110 V and 240 V, particularly for semi-autonomous and remote areas far from Superchargers.

news.title: A Free Solution for Listening to Radio and Music in a Tesla
news.description: The discussion focuses on a solution for listening to radio and music for free in a Tesla.

news.title: Can Tesla Referral Codes Offer a Free FSD Trial?
news.description: A discussion examines the terms and conditions of a Tesla referral program and whether an FSD trial could be included, particularly when purchasing a new car.

news.title: Can Accessories Prevent Tesla Steering Wheel Alerts?
news.description: The discussion concerns accessories designed to eliminate reminders asking the driver to keep their hands on the steering wheel. One participant questions their usefulness and why anyone would want to use them.

news.title: FSD Drives the Wrong Way on a One-Way Street
news.description: An owner explains that their vehicle, in FSD mode, takes a one-way street in the wrong direction when leaving their driveway and asks how to fix the problem.

news.title: Is the 2027 Model Y AWD Standard Limited to 32 A for Charging?
news.description: An owner asks whether the 2027 Model Y Standard AWD has a 32 A onboard charging limit and where to find this information, particularly in the manual.

news.title: Can Tesla’s 2019 Cameras Be Studied in Depth?
news.description: A member describes the architecture of Tesla’s 2019 cameras, with a small dedicated board transmitting video to the controller via coaxial cable and a proprietary protocol, and asks whether anyone has conducted an in-depth analysis.

news.title: The Tesla Wall Connector Button Does Not Open the Charge Port
news.description: An owner says that the button on their Wall Connector does not open the charge port. The discussion notably concerns the Wall Connector version and its antenna receiver.

news.title: What Is the Best Charging Power for a Tesla?
news.description: An owner explains that they charge at 40 A during off-peak hours on a circuit protected by a 50 A breaker in order to benefit from a reduced per-kilowatt-hour rate.

news.title: U.S. Department of Justice investigates Nvidia
news.description: The Department of Justice is conducting three investigations involving Nvidia, including an antitrust case and two others targeting Megaspeed and Supermicro. For now, nothing indicates that criminal charges against Nvidia or Jensen Huang are planned.

news.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to AI Ultra subscribers
news.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon for AI Ultra subscribers, alongside the release of Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

news.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal decisions
news.description: The Gemini Decisions API, based on the Gemini Decision 1 model, is designed for closed-choice decisions such as tool selection, policy checks, and model routing. It can process up to 1,000 independent questions in a single pass and returns probabilities and confidence scores.

news.title: Gartner forecasts more AI-related job creation than job losses
news.description: Gartner forecasts that AI will create 10.6 million jobs and eliminate 8.9 million by 2030, excluding China and India. An additional five million jobs could be deferred as employers delay hiring to assess AI’s impact.

news.title: The B2A economy puts AI agents at the center of business interactions
news.description: AI agents are driving a platform shift from providing answers to executing complex tasks for users, creating a new “B2A” (Business-to-Agent) economy. Companies that treat agents as priority customers could boost growth, while AI-referred traffic is already showing higher engagement and conversion across several sectors.

news.title: Claris Harbor aims to turn Mac fleets into local AI servers
news.description: Apple subsidiary Claris has introduced Harbor, a project aimed at turning Macs equipped with Apple Silicon chips into private AI servers. The product could appeal to companies seeking to keep control of their AI workloads locally, but details remain limited.

news.title: Databricks introduces Genie, an autonomous agent for complex enterprise tasks
news.description: Databricks has introduced Genie, an autonomous AI colleague capable of handling lengthy tasks, coordinating multiple applications, and following organizational rules. Its components provide shared business context, searches combining multiple sources, specialized expertise, and governance for tools, permissions, approvals, and spending.

news.title: Gemini Comes to Apple CarPlay Worldwide
news.description: Google is rolling out the Gemini app on Apple CarPlay worldwide, allowing iOS users to interact with Gemini Live from their car’s display. They can prepare for meetings, review briefings and emails, discover local places, and use Gemini to brainstorm or rehearse a presentation.

news.title: Open standards aim to simplify the development of interoperable AI agents
news.description: Anthropic’s donation of the Model Context Protocol and Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation establishes complementary standards to limit fragmentation in AI-agent ecosystems. MCP standardizes real-time connections to tools and data, while Agent Skills progressively loads the procedural knowledge required.

news.title: AWS Cloud WAN now supports flow logs
news.description: The new feature collects IP addresses, ports, protocols, and traffic volume, among other data. It eliminates the need for users to combine logs from multiple VPCs, accounts, and regions.

news.title: Cognitive science helps developers code better with AI
news.description: Although AI assistants accelerate code generation, developers can rely on cognitive-science principles to preserve their understanding and verify results. The article cites the default mode network, spaced repetition, working-memory retrieval, and scientific debugging.

news.title: Edge0 launches a 145-billion-parameter model for personal computers
news.description: Edge0 has open-sourced Edge0-145B, a 145-billion-parameter model designed to run offline on a personal computer, without an account or subscription. The startup claims more than 80 tokens per second, but no independent benchmark is yet available.

news.title: AgentRun adds memory and self-improvement to open-source AI agents
news.description: GREP.AI has released AgentRun under the Apache-2.0 license to add memory, crash recovery, and guardrails to agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. With learning enabled, agents can retain notes, skills, and procedures after their missions.

news.title: AI agents wrongly claimed credit for a previously known Maya site
news.description: A team of AI agents analyzed satellite images of Mexico and presented as new a Maya site that had already been identified and published the previous year. Archaeologists criticized the announcements for ignoring scientific literature and local knowledge.

news.title: Runway unveils Solaris, which generates interfaces in real time
news.description: Solaris, Runway’s first “Interface World Model,” draws the screen frame by frame and responds directly to clicks instead of coding an application. Runway also uses it to train agents to navigate unfamiliar websites.

news.title: A cosmological model estimates the universe is 26.7 billion years old
news.description: A model proposed by Rajendra Gupta assumes that physical constants evolve slowly and that light loses energy as it travels. It would put the age of the universe at 26.7 billion years, but remains highly marginal and still requires independent verification.

news.title: Phota Labs automatically turns photos into professional-looking shots
news.description: This iOS app, created by two former Adobe employees, scans the camera roll and suggests retouched versions of photos. It learns people’s faces to avoid distorting them and adds an invisible watermark to edited images.

news.title: ElevenLabs launches Scribe v3 Live to improve voice agents
news.description: Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live transcribe conversations with background noise and multiple speakers. The Live version uses context to determine when a person has finished speaking.

news.title: Nectar automates influencer recruitment for brands
news.description: Nectar’s Creator Agent analyzes more than 300 million profiles, their videos, and partnerships to select and contact creators. It also handles contracts, product shipments, and personalized gifts.

news.title: Chinese models appear to carry the signature of Nvidia Blackwell chips
news.description: An analysis of the weights of six Chinese models detected digital traces associated with Nvidia Blackwell chips, which are prohibited from being exported to China. The study does not specify where the chips were located or how they may have been obtained.

news.title: Free Chinese AI models can now hack businesses
news.description: According to Israeli startup Tenzai, freely downloadable Chinese models are capable enough to break into corporate networks. Artificial Analysis is simultaneously observing that progress in the most advanced models is becoming increasingly expensive.

news.title: Trump proposes Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia
news.description: Donald Trump proposed Tim Cook as Jensen Huang’s successor at Nvidia. The former Apple executive remains executive chairman of Apple’s board after handing over the CEO role to John Ternus.

news.title: Australia wants to require independent audits of cutting-edge AI
news.description: The Australian government is proposing mandatory safety rules for companies developing the most advanced models. A regulator could have these models audited by independent experts and impose penalties.

news.title: Nvidia reportedly confirmed that its AI chips can be geolocated
news.description: Nvidia representatives reportedly said privately that it is technically possible to geolocate its AI chips, as provided for by the Chip Security Act. The U.S. Senate is considering incorporating the bill into its defense budget.

news.title: U.S. senator seeks to blacklist memory maker CXMT
news.description: Senator Tom Cotton is calling for CXMT to be placed on the Commerce Department’s blacklist, which would limit its access to U.S. technologies. The Chinese manufacturer grew from 4% to 10% of the global DRAM market in one year and is developing HBM chips.

news.title: Colette Kress seeks to rein in Nvidia’s risky bets
news.description: CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim head of Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s departure. According to people close to her, she did not lead major decisions, and Huang often prevailed when they disagreed.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s departure could affect Asian manufacturers
news.description: Analysts do not expect a short-term disruption involving TSMC, Samsung, or SK Hynix. The main uncertainties concern the long-term product roadmap, which Huang managed directly.

news.title: Chinese laboratories accelerate development of innovative drugs
news.description: Chinese pharmaceutical companies account for at least one-third of innovative drugs in development worldwide and conduct more clinical trials than any other country. They rely mainly on partnerships with Western companies for final development and overseas commercialization.

news.title: mRNA technology opens a new medical chapter
news.description: mRNA technology could produce hundreds of new treatments for various diseases. It can create a vaccine against any pathogen in six to eight weeks and could transform treatments for infectious diseases, rare diseases, and cancer.

news.title: AI-generated “slop” is shifting into design choices
news.description: AI produces significantly less mediocre content, but it has not disappeared. It now manifests itself in design decisions, particularly poor anticipation of how code will be used and limited reuse of existing libraries.

news.title: Ideas once considered bad are becoming relevant again
news.description: Professional experience develops useful intuitions for leaders, but some of them deserve to be reconsidered. Changing circumstances can make ideas once considered bad relevant again.

news.title: Employees at AI companies should unionize
news.description: Safety-conscious employees at AI companies could unionize to gain leverage over their employers. A union could defend their protections, demand greater transparency, and maintain an independent voice in the face of corporate commitments.

news.title: China could have ten times more electricity than the United States
news.description: If current trends continue, China will have ten times more electricity than the United States in ten years.

news.title: Age differences influence the acceleration of AI
news.description: Younger people may be less concerned about AI’s ability to extend life. Older people, with less time remaining, have a stronger incentive to accelerate its development.

news.title: Incident.io details its AI-related spending
news.description: Incident.io’s “effort point” concept is used to analyze AI-related spending.

news.title: Trump mentions Tim Cook as a successor to Jensen Huang
news.description: Donald Trump mentioned Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible successor to Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia. The article highlights his experience succeeding an iconic founder.

news.title: Rust 1.100.0 introduces the never type and new APIs
news.description: The stable Rust 1.100.0 release notably adds the never type, the Allocator and DropGuard APIs, and zero-sized type generation.

news.title: Companies are divided over AI agents’ access to commerce
news.description: Amazon, Booking.com, eBay, Target, Resy, Yelp, and other companies are taking different approaches to third-party agents, ranging from blocking them to approving certain platforms. Companies will therefore choose where and how they participate in the agentic web.

news.title: Visa reveals a high failure rate for agent-driven purchases
news.description: Visa’s benchmark found that 42.8% of agent-driven shopping journeys failed, although some failures still resulted in purchases. Product discovery should therefore not automatically give an agent the power to spend.

news.title: AI reveals that customer loyalty was sometimes built on friction
news.description: AI agents can compare prices, terms, and products every day, threatening loyalty based on customer inertia. Companies must strengthen the value, trust, and experience that remain when comparison becomes easy.

news.title: AI agents are becoming a new distribution channel
news.description: According to McKinsey, large language models can compare far more financial providers than customers previously could. AI removes the friction that protected established players and makes their true loyalty more visible.

news.title: Shopping agents are still making bad decisions
news.description: Visa tested 22 AI models on realistic shopping tasks: 42.8% of executions failed, and 54% of those failures nevertheless resulted in a purchase. AI can therefore remove friction faster than it reduces uncertainty.

news.title: Companies are adopting different strategies toward AI agents
news.description: Retailers, airlines, and platforms are beginning to decide which third-party agents they will accept, limit, or block. This issue is becoming a strategic choice that determines who can participate in customer decisions.

news.title: A Young Founder Named Jensen Huang Benefits from His Namesake’s Troubles
news.description: Jensen Huang, a 24-year-old Singaporean founder, explains why the negative press surrounding Nvidia’s CEO benefits his company.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s Departure Does Not Solve Nvidia’s Problems
news.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation begins a period of instability for Nvidia. Its organizational structure and lack of a succession plan leave many problems to resolve.

news.title: Founder Jensen Huang Had Become Nvidia’s Biggest Risk
news.description: Jensen Huang built the Nvidia empire, but the company’s dependence on him has now become a major risk.

news.title: Nvidia’s Structure Complicates Its Transition After Huang’s Departure
news.description: Flat organizations built around powerful founders can be effective, but they become problematic when their leader is gone.

news.title: Small Investors Keep Buying Nvidia Shares
news.description: Despite Nvidia’s stock decline and Wall Street’s pessimism after Jensen Huang’s resignation, some retail investors are taking advantage of the drop to buy more shares.

news.title: Wall Street Analysts Turn Away from Nvidia
news.description: After revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationships and his departure, Wall Street analysts have become more negative on Nvidia’s stock.

news.title: Warby Parker Launches Smart Glasses to Compete with Meta’s
news.description: Warby Parker’s smart glasses use technologies from Google and Samsung. Business Insider tested them to determine how they differ from Meta’s glasses.

news.title: Silicon Valley Prepares for a Future Without Jensen Huang
news.description: At the Cerebral Valley AI Summit, founders and investors warned that Huang’s departure could hurt startups and destabilize an industry that views Nvidia as its “central bank.”

news.title: The United States Faces a Growing Population Shortage
news.description: Falling birth rates, immigration and tourism are creating a “Great People Shortage.” Areas dependent on newcomers are expected to feel the effects first.

news.title: TikTok Centralizes Its U.S. E-Commerce Operations in China
news.description: TikTok has placed its U.S. e-commerce operations under the responsibility of Chinese executives. Business Insider obtained the organizational chart for the 14 top executives and their teams.

news.title: Instacart Partners with Provi to Supply Bars
news.description: Instacart has partnered with Provi. The platform will offer same-day delivery to bars and restaurants for nonalcoholic items such as mixers and garnishes.

news.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Email for Many Companies
news.description: A Microsoft outage is disrupting email, even as some business executives use it very little.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s Leather Jackets Have Become a Joke
news.description: Jensen Huang’s once-iconic leather jackets are now being mocked following the controversies surrounding the Nvidia leader.

news.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Tool to Address Labor Shortages
news.description: Anthropic is offering a new Claude tool designed to help manufacturers facing labor shortages.

news.title: Flowers Left Outside Nvidia Headquarters After Huang’s Resignation
news.description: Photos show flowers left outside Nvidia headquarters following Jensen Huang’s resignation.

news.title: Amazon’s Ring Flying Camera Raises Questions About Its Target Audience
news.description: The Amazon Ring Drone Cam product has prompted questions about who it is intended for.

news.title: Michael Burry Advises Selling Nvidia Stock
news.description: Investor Michael Burry recommends getting out of Nvidia stock.

news.title: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s Cousin, Leads Nvidia Rival AMD
news.description: Lisa Su, Jensen Huang’s cousin, is the CEO of AMD, an Nvidia competitor.

news.title: Alice Huang Barred from Returning to Singapore
news.description: Singapore says Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive involved in the Nvidia scandal, is not permitted to return to the country.

news.title: RLHF Is Costly Mainly Because of Its Training Loop
news.description: In RLHF, the infrastructure costs of maintaining four models simultaneously during PPO can exceed annotation expenses. DPO reuses the same preference data without a separate reward model, making it a simpler starting point for most teams.

news.title: Cerebras Reports $230.9 Million in Third-Quarter Revenue
news.description: Cerebras reported $230.9 million in third-quarter revenue, up 70%, and raised its full-year guidance.

news.title: FBI Dismantles North Korean Cryptocurrency Theft Campaign
news.description: The FBI disrupted North Korea’s FaceStealer campaign, which used fake Zoom-style meetings featuring recordings of people known to the victims to steal more than $400 million in cryptocurrency.

news.title: Yogurt Summarizes Calls Without Sending a Bot to the Meeting
news.description: Yogurt records calls without having a bot join the meeting, then produces a free summary with next steps assigned to each person. The project is presented as free and open source.

news.title: Pomerado Turns API-Less Websites into Tools for Coding Agents
news.description: Pomerado turns a website without an API, such as a vendor invoice portal, into a tool that a coding agent can use from a single prompt. The service offers a free plan followed by a $50-per-month option.

news.title: Kiln Runs AI Models Directly in the Browser
news.description: Kiln runs conversational, transcription and image models directly in the browser from Hugging Face files, without a server or conversion step. The project is presented as free and open source.

news.title: Spotify DJ Adds Nine Voices and an Option to Turn Off Commentary
news.description: Spotify Premium DJ offers nine new voices and a setting to disable most commentary between songs while retaining personalized recommendations.

news.title: Disney Expands Adobe Partnership for Its Parks, Films and ESPN Content
news.description: Disney is using Adobe’s custom Firefly Foundry models to speed up art design, visual effects and ESPN content. The shorter iteration times also raise questions about work methods and staffing.

news.title: Google Gemini Shows What It Remembers About Users and Lets Them Correct It
news.description: Gemini displays and lets users edit the information it remembers about them in a summary organized into five timestamped categories. However, deleting a memory may not erase the source conversation.

news.title: Microsoft Teams rolls out AI detection of phishing attempts
news.description: Microsoft Teams is rolling out AI-powered detection of impersonation and social engineering in chats, even without a malicious link. Warnings about deepfakes in meetings will follow, but will require third-party configuration.

news.title: Southeast Asian anti-scam hub offers free training
news.description: The Scam Ready ASEAN hub offers free training, an interactive game and country-specific reporting contacts across 11 nations. Scams cost Southeast Asia $23.6 billion.

news.title: Meta AI: features, pricing and user guide
news.description: Meta AI is integrated into Meta’s apps, with features powered by Muse, multiple pricing tiers and privacy controls. The guide covers platform availability and use of Incognito mode, among other topics.
